stem:
A helium atom may be modelled as a nucleus surrounded by two electrons in diametrically opposite circular orbits, each of radius 170 pm, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: State the charge on the nucleus, in terms of the elementary charge *e*.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the electric force between the nucleus and one of the electrons is 1.6 × 10⁻⁸ N.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead: Assume that the force in (b)(ii) is the only force on the electrons.
parts.text: Calculate the speed of the orbiting electrons.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the period of the orbit of the electrons.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.lead: In practice, the orbit of each electron is affected by the presence of the other electron.
parts.text:
For the position of one of the electrons, determine the ratio

$\frac{\text{electric field strength due to the other electron}}{\text{electric field strength due to the nucleus}}$.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Use your answer in (d)(i) to suggest and explain how the orbit of the electron is affected by the presence of the other electron.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: A nucleus is at the centre of a circular dashed electron orbit, with electrons at opposite sides and a radius marked 170 pm.
